summary: Keweenaw tip light: a stone tower lit in 1849, a brick tower of 1866, a 1933 skeletal light still active; reached by boat today.

structures.note: Square brick tower attached to the keeper's dwelling; 35 ft to lantern centre (USLHS); 42 ft (LighthouseFriends). Lamp removed; not an active aid.
Skeletal steel tower, 62 ft; acetylene light, electric from 1937; remains an active aid (LighthouseFriends).
Stone tower 44 ft; replaced 1866; foundations found 1975.
One-and-a-half-story dwelling, 34 by 20 ft, with attached kitchen (LighthouseFriends); the stone dwelling is part of the 2012 NRHP complex.

access.note: No public road access; reached by boat tour from Copper Harbor marina (LighthouseFriends; visitor guide). Seasonal.

corrections.proposed: square brick tower built 1866 (10.7 m to lantern, 35 ft), not active; skeletal steel tower built 1933 (18.9 m, 62 ft), standing and active; the 1848 stone tower (44 ft) is gone and its foundations were found in 1975
corrections.why: The 1848 tower was stone and was replaced in 1866 by a square brick tower; the record's 1848 brick conical tower and its 'standing' status do not match the USLHS record or LighthouseFriends.
Work on the stone tower began in August 1848 and the light commenced operation in spring 1849 (LighthouseFriends); the USLHS place record gives 1849.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: 1848 (record, Rowlett's directory) is the year the stone tower was built; the light began operation in spring 1849 (LighthouseFriends, USLHS).

LighthouseFriends says the light was discontinued after the 1883 season and reopened in 1888; the USLHS 'discontinued 1933' refers to the 1866 lighthouse once the 1933 skeletal tower took over. Both can stand.

notes_for_editor: Unresolved: (1) lens order: fifth (USLHS) vs sixth (LighthouseFriends) in 1856; (2) the station record's characteristic Fl G 6s and focal height 27.4 m could not be verified: LighthouseFriends gives a white flash every three seconds for the 1866 tower after 1919 and a white flash every five seconds for the 1933 skeletal tower; check the current Coast Guard Light List (LLNR 7-15175) before publishing; (3) the 1866 tower's height is 35 ft to lantern (USLHS) and 42 ft (LighthouseFriends). The NRHP nomination (12000305) is not digitised at NPGallery (placeholder); the NRHP detail comes from LighthouseFriends. Michigan.gov's state museum page refused access (HTTP 403). The Chronicling America newspaper search failed repeatedly (loc.gov HTTP 520), so no newspaper search result is used; no newspaper evidence is used. The Bulletin 1925 letter from keeper Charles T. Davis is not used because the OCR interleaves two columns. Charles T. Davis was keeper of the Copper Harbor Range lights in 1917 (Commissioner's report); the Copper Harbor Range lights are a separate station and are not covered here. The Bulletin 1924 index's entry 'Copper Harbor lighthouse reservation donated to Keweenaw County' (p. 139) could not be located in the text, so it is not used. The Bulletin 1923 visibility note (Copper Harbor seen at 34 miles) is garbled in OCR and is not used. Roster lines were matched by name and position in the USLHS record. Henry Corgan's years at Gulf Rock, Point Peninsula and Copper Harbor come from the Bulletin; the dates for those stations are not given. Fact-check pass 2026-10-22: the 1926 Bulletin letter names the keepers' stations (Copper Harbor and Mendota) and the two steamers; the steamers' names are garbled in the OCR, so the story does not give them. LighthouseFriends calls the station 'Peninsula Point' where the Bulletin lists 'Point Peninsula' among Corgan's stations; the story uses LighthouseFriends' form and the identity of the two names is not checked. The Bulletin's 1866 start for Henry Corgan conflicts with LighthouseFriends' age of sixteen; the story states both. The 1970 'early 1970s' restoration event was removed because no source gives a year. The 1892 boathouse is recorded in the Board's report as built by the keeper; LighthouseFriends names Corgan. The LighthouseFriends 'Gulf Rock' spelling in the Bulletin's 1924 list is given as Gull Rock in the story, matching the Bulletin's 1882 entry.
